brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent full hex bases (piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0) joined by a joint bolt, with capped open faces and joints locked; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
addHandle on the top grate cover of the base at 0,0,0 (handle:0,0,0;top).

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for screws and bits
requirements.evidence: Screw bin: hex-bin-full-div3 at 0,0,0 holding M3 screws, nuts and standoffs in its three compartments. Bit bin: hex-bin-full-div2 at 1,0,0 holding a hex key set and a screwdriver.

The grate lid over the screw bin and the handle hide the screw compartments from above (only the bit bin is visible in the view). The bit bin's second compartment holds only the hex key set, and the hex driver set did not fit in it.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell tool caddy: a 3-compartment bin for screws/nuts/standoffs under a grate lid with a carry handle, and an adjacent 2-compartment bit bin holding a hex key set and screwdriver. Open faces are capped and joints locked; the configurator reports no issues. Printing material and strength are not checked by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
